Profile

About

The short version of how a geologist ends up thinking about water.

Shibin is an M.Sc. Geology graduate from the Central University of Punjab, specialising in hydrogeology and hydrochemistry — the chemistry water picks up as it moves through rock, and what that chemistry reveals about where the water has been and where it's headed. His work spans groundwater flow modelling, hydrochemical facies analysis, GIS-based spatial assessment, and water-quality evaluation across field sites in Kerala and Karnataka.

Before Punjab, he completed a B.Sc. (Hons) in Geology at the Central University of Karnataka. Since then he has trained in the field at the Geological Survey of India's centres in Zawar and Raichur, interned at the Centre for Water Resources Development and Management (CWRDM) in Kozhikode, and presented his dissertation research at an international conference.

Core Sample

Dissertation

M.Sc. research, evaluated over four semesters and carried to an international conference.

Evaluation of the Hydrochemical Characteristics along the Groundwater Flow Path in Parappanangadi & Tanur Municipalities, Malappuram District, Kerala

The study area sits along the coastal belt of Malappuram District, in the lower reaches of the Kadalundi River basin. Tanur and Parappanangadi are both low-lying — roughly a metre above mean sea level — bounded by the Arabian Sea to the west, and shaped by a humid tropical monsoon climate with sharply seasonal rainfall. Lateritic formations over crystalline basement rock form the major shallow aquifers here, which makes the system efficient at storing water but also exposed: dense population, rising abstraction, and proximity to the coast leave it vulnerable to hydrochemical alteration and saline intrusion.

  • 01Characterised hydrochemical facies and ionic evolution along the flow path using Piper, Stiff, and Gibbs diagrams.
  • 02Evaluated seawater intrusion risk with Na/Cl, Cl/F, and Revelle indices, identifying zones of elevated salinity.
  • 03Delivered a drinking- and irrigation-suitability assessment using the Water Quality Index and irrigation indices (USSL, Wilcox), flagging zones needing treatment before use.
B.Sc. Dissertation

Hydrochemistry and Suitability Assessment of Water in Dhandoti, Karnataka

Presented under the supervision of Professor M. Prasanth and Dr. Tejaswi Lakkundi (Assistant Professor), Department of Geology, School of Earth Sciences, Central University of Karnataka.

  • 01Assessed drinking- and irrigation-water suitability across groundwater samples using multiple hydrochemical indices.
  • 02Interpreted major-ion chemistry and hydrochemical facies to characterise groundwater quality across the study area.
Casework

Selected Projects

Three projects, distilled to the problem, the method, and what came out of it.

Coastal Groundwater Hydrochemistry — Parappanangadi & Tanur
Problem
Lateritic coastal aquifers in Malappuram District are the main shallow water source for a densely populated area, but rising abstraction and coastal proximity leave them exposed to saline intrusion.
Data
Groundwater samples collected along the flow path across Parappanangadi & Tanur, Kerala.
Methods
Piper, Stiff & Gibbs diagrams; Na/Cl, Cl/F & Revelle indices; WQI and irrigation suitability indices (USSL, Wilcox).
Software
AquaChem, OriginPro, QGIS, IBM SPSS
Key Result
Delivered a complete hydrochemical characterisation and suitability assessment for the coastal flow path, presented at ICRAHES 2026.
Groundwater Flow Modelling — CWRDM Internship
Problem
Understanding aquifer behaviour and recharge patterns to support groundwater exploration and well-siting decisions.
Data
Observation-well data and electrical resistivity (VES) survey results.
Methods
Finite-difference groundwater flow modelling; VES geophysical interpretation.
Software
MODFLOW, ZondIP1D
Key Result
Built a finite-difference flow model and VES-based aquifer geometry assessment that fed directly into CWRDM's technical reporting.
Groundwater Hydrochemistry — Dhandoti, Karnataka
Problem
Assessing whether local groundwater was suitable for drinking and irrigation use in Dhandoti, Karnataka.
Data
Groundwater samples collected across the study area.
Methods
Major-ion chemistry, hydrochemical facies interpretation, multiple suitability indices.
Software
Hydrochemical & statistical analysis
Key Result
Presented findings under the supervision of Prof. M. Prasanth and Dr. Tejaswi Lakkundi, Central University of Karnataka.
